assets.note: Brown bog fowl. Horizontal ovoid body on short scaly legs, S-neck carried forward, tail up at 42 degrees, comb and wattles the only saturated colour. The walk is the real head-bob: the head holds still in space while the body advances under it.

Highland cow. A rectangle on short legs — twice as long as tall, the deliberate opposite of the deer beside it. Horns go OUT then forward then up, spanning wider than the body; the fringe hangs over the eyes; the coat skirt breaks the leg line so it reads heavy and low. Head carried low and grazing, raised only to flee.

Red deer stag. Shallow barrel slung high on long thin legs — the leggy proportion is the whole silhouette. Neck at 45 degrees with a stag's mane, wedge head, antlers sweeping back then tines forward to the player's eye line. Flee is a bound, not a gallop, with the pale rump patch flagged.
